seed: Run `LC_ALL=en_US.ISO8859-1 python3 <the tool's script>` with no arguments, with standard input "Café Ελλάδα\n" as UTF-8 bytes. The input bytes are UTF-8 while the locale is Latin-1, so a tool that uses the locale's encoding reads and writes the wrong bytes. The script is the prototype in work of a command-line tool that reads one title per line on standard input and prints each title's URL slug on its own line. python3 here is Python 3.9.
reference: Standard output is "cafe-ελλαδα\n", encoded as UTF-8, and the exit status is 0.

rubric.check: The input is read as UTF-8 whatever the locale: "Café" gives "cafe" and the Greek word stays letters (the tool's plan: "\"Café\" becomes \"cafe\""; the plan shared by every tool: "A tool reads UTF-8 text on standard input").

The output is written as UTF-8 whatever the locale: standard output is the UTF-8 bytes of "cafe-ελλαδα\n" (the plan shared by every tool: a tool reads UTF-8 text "and writes its result on standard output").
The exit status is 0 (the plan shared by every tool: "A tool exits with status 0 on success").

pattern.context: A command-line tool's plan says it reads and writes UTF-8 text. The tool runs on machines whose locale names another encoding, such as Latin-1, while the bytes it receives are still UTF-8.
pattern.problem: Python opens standard input and output in the locale's encoding. Under a Latin-1 locale each UTF-8 multi-byte character is read as several wrong characters, so accented and non-Latin letters are lost or garbled, and the output is written in Latin-1 or fails on characters Latin-1 cannot hold. Tests run under a UTF-8 locale pass and hide this.
pattern.solution: Read standard input and write standard output as UTF-8 explicitly, independent of the locale. Keep an acceptance case that runs the tool with a non-UTF-8 locale and non-ASCII input.
pattern.consequences: The tool gives the same bytes on every machine. Input that is truly in the locale's encoding, rather than UTF-8, is no longer read correctly; the plan's UTF-8 rule makes that the caller's concern.
